method.label: Find the center using perpendicular lines

annotationRationale: Equal tangent lengths and equal radii place T and O on a perpendicular bisector. Perpendicular slopes and line intersections locate the center, after which coordinate distance gives the radius squared and the circle area.
sourceMethod: Followed the official alternative coordinate solution, finding T on the perpendicular bisector and then intersecting that bisector with the radius line through A. Expanded the line-solving arithmetic.

review.mathCheck: Equal tangent lengths and radii place T and O on \(y=3x-15\), giving \(T=(5,0)\). Intersecting this line with \(x+13y=175\) gives \(O=(37/4,51/4)\), hence \(r^2=170/16=85/8\). The area is \(85\pi/8\), choice C.
review.sourceMethodCheck: This is an independently worded, faithful adaptation of the second official approach on pages 11–12. It reproduces the center intersection and distance calculation, agrees with the supplied figure, and requires no altitude theorem.
review.annotationCheck: The three assessed geometry nodes fit. Perpendicular slopes, line intersection, coordinate distance and circle area appropriately support them. Midpoint, slope and point-slope calculations are shown explicitly; no material explanatory or annotation gap remains.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The exact links for cnm_263, cnm_262, cnm_133, cnm_h172, cnm_h173 and cnm_p192 support the named steps. The partial cnm_h168 link supplies finite-slope perpendicularity; parallel, vertical and coincident-line cases are not demonstrated.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: G-C.A.2 supports tangent-radius perpendicularity; G-CO.C.9 supplies the equidistance locus, although its theorem is applied rather than proved. G-GPE.B.5 supports perpendicular-line equations without proving the slope criterion, and 8.G.B.8 supports coordinate distance. 7.G.B.4 contributes area-formula use only. The accepted G-C.A.4 crosswalk gives no direct evidence for equal tangent lengths here because no tangent construction occurs. G-GPE.B.4/.7 offer coordinate-work overlap without their theorem-proof or polygon-measurement tasks; G-GMD.A.1's formula derivation is absent. cnm_h172 has no supplied US link.
